user_requirements: ROUND 3 — final read-through of a legal draft after material deal changes (not an acquisition analysis). SPA_DRAFT_V4.md is the v4 Agreement for Sale and Purchase of Shares. deal_facts.txt (v2 — READ FIRST) records two material changes made in v4: (1) the Lockhart trustee question is RESOLVED — the trustee parcels are the Vendor's beneficial stake, so Background D now states 1,525 shares per company (1 personal + 1,524 via Lockhart Trustee Services No.222 Limited), clause 1.2 makes the Trustee a definite party, and its execution block is active; (2) a NEW advisory carve-out — the Vendor will continue advising the Companies (QC operations and compliance checking) under a SEPARATE agreement, implemented in v4 as new clause 9.4 (acknowledgement, terms separate) and new clause 10.4(c) (restraint carve-out for services to the Companies). ROUND2_VERIFICATION.md records the previously verified state. Your job: (1) verify the two v4 changes are implemented correctly, completely and consistently — every place the draft previously assumed a conditional trustee (Background D, cl 1.2, cl 3.1(a), cl 4.1(a)-(b), execution blocks, any residual 'if applicable' language) must now read coherently with a definite Trustee party; check the arithmetic (1+1,524=1,525; 15.25% of 10,000); (2) stress-test the advisory carve-out — does cl 10.4(c) create any hole in the restraint beyond services to the Companies themselves (e.g. could the Vendor argue a role with a competitor is 'services to a Company' indirectly)? does cl 9.4 conflict with cl 9.1 (employment ends), cl 9.2 (s149 record, employment-only), cl 9.3 (10-day unpaid handover — is it now redundant or contradictory next to a paid advisory role?), cl 3.1(f) (return of ALL credentials/logins at settlement — but an ongoing QC advisor may need some access), cl 4.3 (pre-settlement discussion ban), and cl 12 (confidentiality — an advisor necessarily receives confidential information)?; (3) confirm the restraint still matches the purchaser's stated intent (no working for a guarding business; no taking clients elsewhere) and that the carve-out cannot swallow it; (4) full read-through for language quality — anything that reads awkwardly, any residual conditional/hedged wording that should now be definite, any gendered pronoun (the Vendor is male; the draft should use 'the Vendor' throughout — flag ANY she/her), numbering and cross-references after the 9.4 insertion; (5) regulatory-integrity re-confirmation. Output: verification of the two v4 changes, then findings with severity (BLOCKER/RECOMMENDED/OPTIONAL) and exact fix wording, then the final sign-readiness verdict and the remaining placeholder list.
